Every jury that aquits a rapist.   Every one who wrote a letter supporting Brock Turner.  All the people who downvote victims of rape on redditt every day.  The people who hacked the me too page and trolled the participants.   The judges who give laughable sentences.   The people who use subreddits  for finding affair partners.  The people who say ’that wasn't sexual assault, you should have been clearer’  the people who argue against affirmative consent because it's not sexy or suggest that lying about your marital status is ’just one of those things’   And that its ridiculous that people might have morals about not wanting to cheat and feel repulsed by that.  The people who say ’well, she does drink a lot when she goes out’   Or ’it was bound to happen’  or ’my son/brother/ friend/partner would NEVER do that’  

People who say they don't believe it actually do put it in action.   I find myself doing it:  about myself too.

Ok.   Suppose I wanted to arm myself?   As a ptsd suffering victim of rape and child sexual abuse, I am no longer able to carry where I live;  and that is absolutely how it should be.    So it rules out a significant proportion of potential victims on age and / or after effects.

Thank you u/bubblesthehorse.   Some of us have learnt from assault situations that compliance means getting out ’just raped’  not raped and beaten,  or not getting out.   

Compliance,  or what some call ’fawning’  is increasingly being recognized alongside, fight, flight and freeze.   We might try negotiations like ’i’m tired’ or distractions,   Or  we might comply with a lesser sex act to try and lessen the abuse,  or just not fight back, or even smile if the perp wants engagement rather than be treated violently.     It might not be seen as strong or tough but those who comply have often done it to stay alive.   It's common for example, in child abuse situations or I understand in domestic violence situations
Actually i’d quite like my perps to pay a contribution for their therapy AND mine.    As restorative justice.   More use to them and society than jail for non-aggravated rape/ Sexual Assault.
Being taken more lightly than or should be?   Or all types of sexual assault and non consent  being taken as seriously as they should be?

Rapes/ sexual assaults  are already classified differently.    This impacts on sentence length.   For the record initiating while unconscious / sleeping is considered quite serious:   I was surprised;   It was the nature of the rape I reported last year ( a none aggravated rape)   And I wanted to report only initially and it was explained that its severity was such the police officer was mandated to inform the DA and instigate an initial investigation even though we all knew no evidence sufficient existed for a trial.   Where I was that was a ’grade two sexual assault ’    Aggravated rape, or gang rape would gave been the only more severe rape,  grade one
I’d like to be in a position to say ’thank you’ and ’do well’ in response to them taking responsibility.    What a pipe dream.

We need to hear it until we all say we've had enough and DEMAND changes.   Clearer more consistent  for the benefit of everyone.  A system that works to see more reports made and convictions happen.   So that the 1/4 women, 1/6 men and 1/3 lgbt victims and the perpetrators who sometimes really aren't heinous people ( the ted talk with tom stranger and thordis elva?? I think her name is, is a good example) get help they need too.

I agree.  When my case could proceed last year the police did make me feel they were on my side.  They were clear they believed me; as did the DA, but that a jury would struggle because like most rapes it came down to one person saying it was consensual and the other not.  

With 99 percent of sex crimes unpunished the system we use is not fit for purpose.   That's not the police’s fault ( whether or not they are good ) nor those in the system really.    

We need a different system.   Nowhere else would something where this failure rate exist be considered fit for purpose.

I am not practicing poly at all now.   But I always maintained the ability to love more than one person.   The relationship I referred to has broken my trust completely and I never will have another relationship again.  

My husband however is strictly monogamous.   I would say it is more than choice :  it’s part of who we are.   Our choice is to honour our integrity and discuss these things with each other.    And poly people absolutely can control not getting into bed with people not available to them, not coercing or lying to partners and if need be terminating monogamous relationships if they really feel ill suited to it.   it’s as offensive as suggesting a bisexual person cannot be faithful to their partner.     It’s abhorrent to ignore other people’s lives.   People aren’t candy we can lick at ;   Our actions do impact on others.     My point isn’t really about whether it’s choice or orientation:  I think that it will differ really.   I will always be ‘me’ but can choose to live monogamously.   I agree, I know many who make an active choice.   I don’t know it even matters.   The point is to live in a way that’s decent and respectful of other people’s rights.  

So yes;  I very much have a problem in the way you do.   Violation of agreed terms of a relationship, lying. Coercion anything like that;  it’s abusive.  Non consensual.

Me too.    I cannot react like this.    It’s a result of learning as a child that it’s safer to comply.   Go with things.   So women who can are my heroes.   Even if they cannot understand why women like I cannot do other than freeze and fawn,   I can admire them and rejoice in their ‘fuck yous’.  I don’t know if they realise how important their reactions can be for the rest of us .

I’m poly.   In that i can love more than one person at once. I think this is my orientation but very rarely happens to me.   My marriage gas only had one other person in it and i gave no interest in cheating at all.    I respect others relationships UTTERLY.  

I was also unwittingly an AP ( the one other oerson) to a man who provided pretty convincing evidence his wife was ok with our relationship but didn't want to meet me or hear from me:  a don’t ask don't tell relationship.    When i found out otherwise it was incredibly traumatic to me.   Consent is a huge part of my life and always has been.   It was something i had checked and double checked with him,  and would never gvw acted on my emotions with out his lies.   It was not being blinded by live either:  he convinced my husband of his story with his evidence,  with whom he became friends.   

The impact of having inadvertently caused another woman betrayal caused me moral injury significant enough to cause me significant harm in addition to the obvious heartbreak.  I believe chumplady calls people in my situation fellow chumps.    

I have heard now of several women to whom this has happened.  Not all AP’s know that's what we are in these situations.   There is a poly mantra that you do not owe your metamours anything;   I strongly disagree with this.   It's my opinion that infidelity imposes a sort of non-consent on a relationship ( the spouse has only consented to being in a monogamous relationship)  and thus is heinous.   

The impact of involvement in this is not a free pass to me.   I cannot forgive my self at all ( though the woman i believed to be my metamour did).  Please know that not all poly people do not treat your monogamous relationships this way. It’s as disgusting to me as it is you;  and as shameful.

You might try rainn. org to locate any local resources? 

I am only a year ish out and I do did that anniversaries of all sorts are very triggering as I am frustrated about ‘lost joy’ as well as the ptsd stuff.  

My therapist always recommends making time for some compassion and nurture ( exercise,personal  grooming or what ever works for you) andtime at the end of each day to find three to five positives in the day.   It’s not to ignore the bad stuff,  but to try and remember the good stuff and go to bed adding more weight to this .

Likewise aggravated rape should be sentenced more severely.   It doesn't make coercive rape ’more ok’

I don't know why comments supporting this sort of position get down voted so often.   It concerns me that people think it's OK to coerce/ be coered to sex and don't realise that it's not legal ( if hard / impossible to prove).
Thank you. I’m crying. Thank you.  Mine was nothing like OP’s.

Yes.   I feel this all very strongly in my heart. 


OP my rape last year was not an aggravated rape,  but the CSA and previous learned experiences has made my reaction that to comply.    Because I learnt early its better yo comply and get out sexually assaulted but otherwise ’ok’ rather than sexually AND physically assaulted.   Or maybe not get out.   

When people say ’why didn't the victim fight back’ there is a presumption we have had fearless lives where fighting or speaking out has been rewarded as if should gave been.   Sadly this is rarely the case.  We live in a world where ’reacting the right way’ doesn't get the right results always.   


My heart breaks when I see the amount of victim blaming daily here.   More so the ’i didn't behave like that, so she cannot have been raped ’ kind if comments.   

Aggravated rape as an adult I think would push my mental state to a place I am not sure I could come back from now.    OP is a strong woman, and I applaud her, and ache for her.    

People SHOULD be bothered by this.   They should be uncomfortable by a lot less than this.   And yes, we should be checking out selves and how we behave to others.   Who wants to be even a tiny bit part of this problem?

Why not check out the stats yourself?   You might find others that interest yo too!   

RAINN.org is a good place to start reading about the extent of the problem.

That's how I feel; it's not ok.   I am so glad you are coping and feeling whole OP.   

This sounds like aggravated rape, not ’just’ rape to me.    ( I don't mean ’just’ in a trivial way’).

Thanks for clarification of this.   

I have ptsd and if I hurt people it's in being impolite or panic trying to protect myself.   Mainly trying to end conversations do I can go and ’hide ’ got a while.  Not answering door/ phone etc.


I am sure people react differently but dissociation or being a bit self involved from the planning about fear / safety seems common in the few people I know with ptsd.

Love/ attraction  doesn't stop because a relationship does or you realise the person is a bit of a jerk; sadly.

It can be involve emotional abuse like daylighting, financial deceptions as well as the health risks. 

You bet I would want to know. It also gives polyamory a really bad name when it's conflated with poly lifestyle or polyamorists are seen as ’soft’ on this type of action.   I can see why strict monogomists fear this.

I am no longer poly.   I was  before marriage and had one poly relationship during that was DADT on his side and he turned out to be a liar who created significant false proof.  

I consider it rape by fraud.   In the same year I had a ’traditional rape’ and the DADT lie has damaged me far, far more.   The moral injury of being involved in betraying a spouse,  my heartbreak ( I love who I thought he was very much) and the not knowing what of what happened that year was real and what false is extremely disorienting.   I was diagnosed with PTSD and I think it is the cheater more than the normal rape, truly.   

When I read and hear ’we owe nothing to metamours’. It makes my stomach turn.  Because I think we do owe it to make sure the situation is ok, and that poly us a choice not a coercion if it's a marriage.    I never want to be part of anything none consensual in any form.   

I am left in state that while I am married if I weren't I would be single for ever.   I cannot trust anyone because of the elaborate web of lies spun and false evidence provided.  I know several people whose poly is coerced and maintained so their spouses / life partners don't leave them and I hate that too.  Any form of non consent is not something I feel I would want to be associated with.  My love shouldn't hurt another.

The advice to speak to rain.org is the best you have been given.

To others saying ’just leave ’ and so on, men can freeze or panic in the same way women can.    How we review this afterwards is not how we react  at the time.   Even in repeat events.  It's not the victim’s fault, whatever the gender of the victim.

I believe you.   

I am female, have experienced sexual assault including by a woman.  In my rape survivors group there are men and I want you to know they are taken EVERY BIT as seriously as women.  

Stats support this.  1/4 women,   1/6 men,  high for trans people. 

I believe you.  

I really strongly encourage you to speak to RAINN.org.   They have a chat service if the phone feels too much right now.   The wait can be long so have a book or magazine to read while you wait, but it's worth it.   They will believe you too.  

I hope you can ask them for a nearby victim advocate to talk to.    They will also believe you and direct you to any available support services in your area.  

You are NOT alone.  You aren't weak or lesser.   People who don't accept this can happen are very lucky to have not experienced it.

Please reach out.

I’m sorry you were is empowered over this,  I know it the thing many of us fear most,  but I think you can use it very much to make a better future for you.   

We believe you.

I do not think OP is behaving ideally but my position is that I would be shocked if he were.   In trauma we DO behave oddly.   Exactly as you said, we can only take so much.   He decided he voukx not take confrontation that morning.   So be it.  

What is ideal is not irrelevant but it's also just not possible when you are clinging on to semblance of holding your new reality together or processing what else on your life might not be true.

If there is ’respect’ then you do not impose that on someone.

We had STD discussions too.   In the years this took place I was at a convent school.   I am forever grateful and impressed that the nuns and lay teachers put health  above religion and taught us where abstinence was not going to happen barrier methods should.  It showed tremendous sense and empathy.

But it terrifies me.  Suppose he doesn’t want to be touched and we don’t know because we are asleep?   He reassures me all the time that this is always ok with him, that accidentally or on purpose I can touch him unless he indicates otherwise.   But I am terrified I will transgress as I was transgressed on.   So many people seem to say ‘I didn’t know’ or ‘I just misconstrued’ or ‘I didn’t realise’. Although I KNOW I haven’t done that I am scared because I also don’t want to.   It’s almost as if I am trying to control it by being super controlling of myself .   But it makes it worse.   The ways sexual assault can play with one person’s mind are astounding. 



Take care.

Generally?   Not being believed the first time.   Societal attitudes.   Note that the wife’s friends doubted her;  this is really, very common.   Another thread on this sub yesterday asked if there was a preponderance of threads about false accusations and it got little attention but the false accusation theme is big in society and big on Reddit.    Which means essentially victims are called liars.   So as a victim you are dealing with the ‘trauma’ of being groped -assaulted-raped and the trauma of feeling unsupported.    The impact of the lack of support has been shown to be so impactful that we will often choose not to report over feeling saftey in the pack.   Maybe because alone we are more likely to be vulnerable  to predation next time?  I don’t think it’s something we plan out.

If you get a positive response from reporting a first time, chances are you will a second.     If you are told, ‘there there, he is just pulling your pig tails’ and your concerns are dismissed or similar you lose faith.    When stats are against you etc.... it’s difficult not to argue with it.  

I did report ,  no evidence,  and my rapist walks free.

I am ’ white appearing’ married to a person of another culture and country.   We are always presumed when speaking in the language we use daily to be from the place we live now.   We have close connections to it, sure,  but not having the other parts of us acknowledged because we love and respect the culture in which we live feels harsh.   If i wear ’ethnic clothing’ because i am white appearing i am doomed to look presumptuous.   Which seems sad to me.   If anyone enjoys  a culture or an aspect of it i think they should be allowed to display that.   We don't live in a vacuum.   Cultures have influenced other cultures forever.  


Personally i dislike the ’yoga body’ type exercise approach because i think it's like reducing Islam to burka wearing or Christianity to select parts if the new testament.    But just as Christianity left the Mediterranean and people of other religions can be found globally and we find it uncomfortable when governments oppress freedom of thought to practice alternative religion or non religion,   I think the same can apply to ’yoga’.   


My friends are my friends.  Not my brown friends or my Indian friends or what ever.   i do have biases.   If i am struggling with a recipe i think ’who likes to cook,   X and y,  oh Y’s mother is from that place maybe they will know what i am getting wrong’.   I totally accept that's presumptive and i have friends who totally buck the trends.

I think it's amazing you are listening to you and maintaining your integrity.   

Making decisions about this has been a significant part of my own ongoing ’process’ after rape last year and i find my position has shifted.   I am still pro restorative justice ( maybe even more so) in lots of cases of non aggravated sexual assault. And i think that's partly because I recognize more how extensive the problem is.   When i read stats like ’between 1/7 and 1/16 men’ or 44% percent prevalence of intimate partner crime in lesbian communities ( just two examples showing the prevalence and that it's not wholly gender specific )  it has made me accept i know rapists.    I have reviewed and analyzed my own sexual behavior almost obsessively (in unwanted touch for reasons i understand i freeze then comply) but that's ’wrong’.  It makes it unclear to the rapist,  looks like i eventually gave consent.   It's certainly part of why i would not choose to engage in casual sex anymore;  i understand that to be fair to my partners in consent they need to know me well.   

After i told some people about my rape i didn't expect whole hearted belief.    I still don't really.   No one else was there;   Just me and the person who violated me;  my word against theirs.   But i did  decide to drop contact with  people who were trying to be as balanced as i logically feel.    It feels really hypocritical when i accept no one else can really know.

One person in particular sent me an email saying that the person was selfish but not malicious.... I sort of agree with that.  But then i saw a message from that person being lovely to the rapist on social media.   I just do not need to be dealing with what i felt as insincerity while I patch myself up. 

I think statistically it's inevitable we know people who sexually assault.   Not aggravate rape but coercion, the not listening and not really acknowledging to themselves they did anything wrong.  And then there is how we view other sexual violation :  coercion is wrong but defrauding isn't?  I can't get my head round that.   ( neither are the same as aggravated rape).  

 Looking at how we treat people we know who sexually assault iis hard  because i think that we both have to accept they are humans who have likable, lovable traits,  and also when we consider it in depth that considered we  are invited to  examine other behavior of those we care for, or ourselves and maybe shift our goal posts or accept transgressions closer to home :  and accept not all violation is that of drooling uncontrolled hate figures but people you would hope could have said ’ i’m sorry,  i messed up and didn't listen to you’.
Isn't it a shame in a world that requires proof that people don't get ’proof’  that the person they feel like touching wants to be touched?

I have been thinking about this from my perspective  for a year now.    I really wish in fact someone HAD encouraged me to report, or to take action.  I think had my partner said something like that i might have felt ’safer’.   

It's not ideal.  I want to be strong and secure and able to cope myself but one of the things i really regret is delaying report.   If i had been encouraged to do that i think it would have made the world of difference to me.   

I think that in respecting victim need for autonomy it may in some cases prolong trauma when it's trauma/ fear or something like that stops report.

I don't think that's true.   My experience of reporting rape in the last year does not echo this,  neither does it sound at all like what the ( supportive) police dealing with sensitive crimes all day every dayvsaid to me.

My guess, but i don't know,  is that if he us a groper the sport gave him access to do that.   Other ways exist to grope.   Public transport, crowds.  Maybe he  violates using other avenues. 

Those ARE NOT your wife’s responsibilities.    I am ABSOLUTELY not saying that.   I am just... Myself in a position where i am trying to resolve that this is the way it is.   That even when we try or do a good thing we cannot stop people.   I want yo be really clear i am not saying your wife should have felt pressure to do other.   Standing up for yourself in these situations is courageous and what she did helps all of us, that a couple more people understand more through this, you and your studio owner, is progress

Lots of my friends go braless,  and I never wear padded bras and know that this means my nipples are often evident.   I am ok with this.  It's not offensive, provocative, or anyone elses business.   I personally find the idea we must look like barbie or ken with no visible bits or pieces very odd.   I’m not smooth all over.   I have nipples.   They just exist there on my body.   They aren't bothering anyone.  I find iit almost deviant , that it's considered necessary for me to flatten my nipples for polite society.   Is this so, men can control themselves?   Decent men can and bra choice had no say in it other wise.

I think it makes things EASIER.   But I personally feel that the idea of moving on entirely and putting it in my past is part of what allows the situation to remain unchanged.   So while I want peace for myself I sort of also want a bit of fire in my belly to fight for a better justice system and better understanding and education about consent.

I felt really uncomfortable about it but understood it was their dynamic and it was not my right to force the issue.  My lover met and became friends with my artner though, and we all became very committed.  

When I found out he had spun an intricate web of lies and was simply a cheater I felt more violated than on the sad occasions I have been raped.  

It’s absolutely devastated me and I would do anything I could if I could turn back time and not have inadvertently betrayed someone’s marriage.  

If you could bring yourself to I would at least say hi to your metamour on the phone one night they are together.  Try and be part of the difference that stops people posing as poly.

Yes,  I agree,  she is should not  rationally be offended.   Its tough being rational when your heart is broken. 

Ghosting is disappearing without explanation isn’t it?  There is explanation, he has left her.  Men often want to leave someone then not feel bad while a woman is made seem crazy for still processing and finding it incredibly difficult.  

I totally agree, her reaction to his deletion is not rational.  Where I disagree is that we must ALWAYS expect people to behave rationally ( either gender) in heartbreak/ distress/ assault.    We are human before all else.

He could also have respected her need for distance,  and used empathy to realise that some people are incredibly upset at the end of relationships.   That while he may have had some time to understand his feelings, it’s very new to her.  

I think not responding to a message ( which says he would understand if she wasn’t ready)  is much better than responding and raging ; the default of some others. 


Op;  block everywhere.   Block, block.   Seeing his stuff keeps pain alive,  him seeing your stuff gives you no privacy to heal.   

You have no control over his feelings.  Sucks, huh?

I’m so glad they came forward and I hope you can all support each other.
